parameters.content:
## Incident Commander

### How it works

A multi-agent DevOps incident commander. It intakes incidents from a schedule sweep, a webhook (alertmanager/monitoring), or a manual test run, then loops through an incident queue. For each incident it gathers diagnostics (metrics + recent deploys), runs a Triage Agent (Claude) to classify severity and likely root cause, runs a Remediation Planner Agent (Claude) to propose a runbook action and risk level, gates the action behind human approval when risk or severity warrants it, executes the runbook when clear, drafts a stakeholder update with a Communications Agent (Claude), posts it to Slack, and logs the outcome. A separate Approval Callback webhook lets a human approve a pending high-risk action asynchronously. When the queue empties, it builds and sends a final incident digest.

### Setup steps

- Configure the schedule interval and enable the intake webhook if alerts will be pushed in from your monitoring/alerting stack.
- Set monitoring, deploy-history, incident-manager, runbook-execution, Slack, and status-page URLs in the configuration node.
- Add credentials/headers for monitoring, incident manager, runbook engine, Anthropic Claude API, and Slack.
- Tune autoRemediateMaxSeverity, maxIncidentsPerRun, and the risk logic in 'Parse Remediation Plan' to match your escalation policy.
- Wire the Approval Callback webhook URL into your Slack approval button / approval UI so approvers can trigger execution.
- Test with the manual trigger and a single sample incident before enabling the schedule.

### Customization

Adjust the three agent system prompts (Triage, Remediation Planner, Communications), the approval risk thresholds, and the runbook action vocabulary (restart_service, scale_up, rollback_deploy, failover, clear_cache, feature_flag_disable, no_action_monitor) to match your stack.

## Trigger intake

Starts the workflow from a periodic sweep for open incidents, a webhook that receives pushed alerts (Alertmanager / Datadog / PagerDuty), or a manual test run, then normalizes the incoming payload into a common shape.

## Configure run mode

Applies workflow settings (thresholds, endpoints, model), determines whether this is an ad hoc single-incident run or a sweep of open incidents, and branches accordingly.

## Build incident queue

Creates the processing queue either from the single incident supplied by the trigger or by fetching all open incidents from the incident manager and converting them into queued work items.

## Advance incident queue

Pulls the next incident off the queue and decides whether to continue the diagnosis pipeline or finish the run because the queue is empty or the per-run cap was hit.

## Gather diagnostics

Pulls a recent metrics snapshot and recent deploys for the affected service and merges them into one diagnostics bundle for the agents to reason over.

## Triage + remediation planning agents

A Triage Agent (Claude) classifies severity, likely root cause, and affected components. A Remediation Planner Agent (Claude) then proposes one concrete runbook action and a risk level for taking it automatically.

## Approval gate + execution

High/medium risk actions, or actions on incidents more urgent than the configured auto-remediate threshold, trigger a Slack approval request and are marked pending (executed later via the Approval Callback webhook, below). Low-risk actions execute immediately against the runbook engine.

## Communications + logging

A Communications Agent (Claude) drafts a concise stakeholder status update reflecting whatever happened (executed / pending approval). The update posts to Slack, the full outcome logs to the incident record, and the loop advances to the next incident.

## Send final digest

Builds the run's incident digest once the queue is empty, posts it to Slack, and returns it to the webhook caller.

## Approval callback (async human-in-the-loop)

A second entry point. When a human approves (or declines) a pending remediation from Slack, this webhook fires the runbook action for real, notifies the incident channel, and responds to whatever called it. This is separate from the main loop above so approval doesn't have to block the workflow run.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 800, system: 'You are an SRE incident triage agent. You are given raw metrics, recent deploys, and an initial alert description for one incident. Classify the severity, identify the most likely root cause hypothesis, list affected components, and flag whether a recent deploy is a plausible trigger. You do not have log-level detail beyond what is provided; be explicit about your confidence. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {"severity": string, "confidence": number (0-100), "likelyRootCause": string, "affectedComponents": [string], "suspectDeploy": {"version": string, "reason": string} | null, "summary": string}.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Incident ID: ' + $json.currentIncidentId + '
Service: ' + $json.currentService + '
Reported severity: ' + $json.currentSeverity + '
Alert source: ' + $json.currentSource + '
Alert description: ' + $json.currentDescription + '
Metrics snapshot: ' + JSON.stringify($json.metricsSnapshot) + '
Recent deploys: ' + JSON.stringify($json.recentDeploys) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 800, system: 'You are an SRE remediation planning agent. Given a triage assessment for one incident, propose the single best next remediation action from common runbook categories (restart_service, scale_up, rollback_deploy, failover, clear_cache, feature_flag_disable, no_action_monitor), plus a risk level for taking that action automatically without a human. High risk actions include anything touching production data, irreversible rollbacks on an unclear root cause, or actions on P1 incidents with low confidence root cause. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {"action": string, "actionParams": object, "riskLevel": string ("low"|"medium"|"high"), "riskReason": string, "rollbackPlan": string, "reasoning": string}.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Incident ID: ' + $json.currentIncidentId + '
Service: ' + $json.currentService + '
Reported severity: ' + $json.currentSeverity + '
Triage assessment: ' + JSON.stringify($json.triage) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ text: '⚠️ Approval needed for "' + $json.currentIncidentId + '" (' + $json.currentService + ', ' + $json.currentSeverity + ')
Proposed action: ' + $json.remediationPlan.action + '
Risk: ' + $json.remediationPlan.riskLevel + ' - ' + $json.remediationPlan.riskReason + '
Reasoning: ' + $json.remediationPlan.reasoning + '
Approve via the incident commander approval callback with this incidentId.' }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 500, system: 'You are an incident communications agent. Given the triage assessment, the remediation plan, and whether it was executed or is pending human approval, draft a concise stakeholder-facing status update (2-4 sentences) suitable for a status page or Slack channel, in a calm and factual tone. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {"statusUpdate": string, "internalNote": string, "nextCheckInMinutes": number}.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Incident ID: ' + $json.currentIncidentId + '
Service: ' + $json.currentService + '
Reported severity: ' + $json.currentSeverity + '
Triage summary: ' + $json.triage.summary + '
Remediation action: ' + $json.remediationPlan.action + '
Remediation status: ' + $json.remediationStatus } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ incidentId: $json.currentIncidentId, service: $json.currentService, severity: $json.currentSeverity, triage: $json.triage, remediationPlan: $json.remediationPlan, remediationStatus: $json.remediationStatus, communications: $json.communicationsDraft, loggedAt: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ text: '\ud83e\uddef Incident Commander digest: ' + $json.incidentsProcessed + ' incident(s) processed, ' + $json.autoRemediatedCount + ' remediated, ' + $json.pendingApprovalCount + ' pending approval. By severity: ' + JSON.stringify($json.bySeverity) }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ incidentId: $json.incidentId, service: $json.service, action: $json.action, actionParams: $json.actionParams, approvedBy: $json.approvedBy }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ text: '\u2705 Approved remediation executed for \"' + $('Parse Approval Callback').first().json.incidentId + '\" by ' + $('Parse Approval Callback').first().json.approvedBy + '. Action: ' + $('Parse Approval Callback').first().json.action }) }}
